newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa May new car sales fall 21.2 percent yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa May new car sales fall 21.2 percent yr/yr.

text.p: New car sales slumped 21.2 percent year-on-year in May to 19,375 units but still rose 0.7 percent from April's 19,232 units, the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa said on Wednesday.
The association said in a statement the recent slowdown in new car and commercial vehicle sales had gained further momentum in May, reflecting a general levelling off in the economy.

"Growth momentum has slowed significantly in recent months as a result of high levels of indebtedness, exceptionally high interest rates and the downturn in business conditions in many sectors of the economy," Naamsa said.
In aggregate terms, new vehicle sales for the first five months of the year had fallen behind aggregate sales during the corresponding five months in 1996, declining 3.3 percent.

Should interest rates remain high during the second half of 1997 and if there was no pick up in economic activity, this year's new vehicle sales levels were unlikely to match those of 1996, Naamsa said.
The organisation first predicted in January that 1997 new car sales were likely to fall to 242,000 from 249,884 in 1996.

In sharp contrast to weakness in the domestic market, total exports of South African produced vehicles continued their strong trend in the first four months of the year, soaring 125.0 percent compared with the same period in 1996.
Volkswagen of South Africa marketing director Graham Hardy said the May figures showed a clear softening in the market despite the introduction of new models at very competitive prices.
Hardy said there were no immediate prospects for improvement in demand unless underlying economic conditions improved, possibly in the fourth quarter of the year.
